artists.biography: Faces (sometimes erroneously known as The Faces) are an English rock band formed in 1969 by members of Small Faces after Steve Marriott left that group to form Humble Pie. The remaining Small Faces - Ian McLagan (keyboards), Ronnie Lane (bass), and Kenney Jones (drums & percussion) - were joined by Ronnie Wood (guitar) and Rod Stewart (lead vocals), both from The Jeff Beck Group, and the new line-up was renamed Faces.

Faces.biography: Faces (sometimes erroneously known as The Faces) are an English rock band formed in 1969 by members of Small Faces after Steve Marriott left that group to form Humble Pie. The remaining Small Faces - Ian McLagan (keyboards), Ronnie Lane (bass), and Kenney Jones (drums & percussion) - were joined by Ronnie Wood (guitar) and Rod Stewart (lead vocals), both from The Jeff Beck Group, and the new line-up was renamed Faces.

perplexity.description:
The album The Best Of The Faces is a 1977 compilation by the British rock band Faces, released on the Riva label. It serves as a retrospective collection highlighting the band's blend of rock and pop, capturing their raw, energetic style characterized by Rod Stewart's distinctive vocals and Ronnie Wood's gritty guitar work. This compilation follows the band's four studio albums released between 1970 and 1973, including First Step, Long Player, A Nod Is As Good As a Wink... to a Blind Horse, and Ooh La La, and it showcases some of their most popular and enduring tracks from that period.

Positioned as a key summary of Faces' career after their disbandment in 1975, The Best Of The Faces offers listeners a concise overview of the band's influential sound that combined blues-rock with a loose, party-like atmosphere. While not as comprehensive as later box sets, this album was significant in maintaining the band's legacy during the late 1970s. Critically, Faces were praised for their spirited performances and songwriting, with this compilation reinforcing their status as a seminal British rock group of the early 1970s. Commercially, the album helped sustain interest in the band’s catalog post-breakup, particularly in the UK and Europe where it was primarily released.
